body.p: REMARKS
This Amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated November 16, 2022.
Applicant has amended claims 1, 3, 4, 11-13, 18, 20, 27, and 29, canceled claims 2 and 19, and added new claims 31 and 32. Claims 1, 3-18, and 20-32 are pending upon entry of this Amendment.

A telephonic interview was conducted on January 24, 2023, between Applicant's undersigned representative, and Examiners Michael J. Lau and Carl Layno. The parties discussed the rejection of independent claim 1 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2005/0115561 by Stahmann et al. (hereinafter, "Stahmann"). Applicant's representative proposed amendments to claim 1 similar to those presented in this Amendment. The Examiners identified additional portions of Stahmann (e.g., paragraphs [1320]-[1321] and [1516]-[1517]) that allegedly disclose subject matter of amended claim 1. No agreement was reached, and no other issues were discussed, nor items presented.
The Office Action rejected claims 1-30 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:
" Claims 1-16 and 18-30 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Stahmann;
and
" Claim 17 was rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Stahmann in view of U.S.
Publication No. 2012/0283705 by Lee et al. (hereinafter, "Lee").

Without conceding the merits of the rejections, and in the interest of advancing prosecution to an indication of allowance, Applicant has amended the claims. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections to the extent the rejections may be considered applicable to the claims as amended. The applied references, alone or in any proper combination, fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's amended claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
For example, Stahmann fails to disclose or suggest "a plurality of electrodes on [a]
housing, wherein [an] ICM is configured to sense an electrocardiogram (ECG) of [a] patient via

the plurality of electrodes," as recited by independent claim 1, or the similar recitations of amended independent claims 18, 27, and 29. The Office Action cited to electrodes 210 and paragraphs [0217] and [0376] of Stahmann as allegedly disclosing a plurality of electrodes used to sense an ECG.1 In Stahmann, reference number 210 refers to a cardiac device in FIGS. 2A and 2B, rather than electrodes. Directly contrary to a plurality of electrodes on a housing of an ICM, paragraph [0217] of Stahmann describes, inter alia, "[t]he intracardiac lead system 410 includes one or more electrodes configured to sense electrical activity of the heart . ..." Paragraph [0376] of Stahmann is completely unrelated to ECG sensing or electrodes. In FIGS. 5C-5E, Stahmann depicts housing 531 of ITCS 500, which the Office Action relied on as allegedly meeting other requirements of a housing in Applicant's claims, as having a single electrode 533, rather than a plurality of electrodes. Moreover, Stahmann does not suggest that ITCS 500 is configured to sense an ECG via a plurality electrodes on housing 531.
Stahmann also does not disclose or suggest "processing circuitry configured to:

periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of [] heart sounds or [an] ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG; output trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters at the remote computing device; and determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters," as recited by amended claim 1, or the similar recitations of amended independent claims 18, 27, and 29.
In rejecting previously presented claims 2 and 19, the Office Action alleged that

paragraph [0972] of Stahmann discloses determining whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of trends of periodically determined values of physiological parameters. Paragraph [0972] of Stahmann does not mention a heart failure event, much less determining whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of trends of values of a plurality of physiological parameters determined based on an ECG and heart sounds. During the Examiner Interview, the Examiners identified paragraphs
1 Office Action dated November 16, 2022, pg. 4.

[1320]-[1321] and [1516]-[1517] as allegedly being relevant to this claim feature. However, paragraphs [1320]-[1321] and [1516]-[1517] do not discuss heart failure, much less "processing circuitry configured to ... determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of [] trends of [] values of [] physiological parameters [periodically determined based on heart sounds and an ECG]," as recited by claim 1, or the similar recitations of independent claims 18, 27, and 29.
For at least the reasons discussed above, independent claims 1, 18, 27, and 29 are

patentable over the applied references. The dependent claims, i.e., claims 3-17, 20-26, 28, and 30, incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.2 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable.

Moreover, the dependent claims include a number of features likewise not disclosed or suggested by the applied references. For example, the applied references fail to disclose or suggest "the indication of the heart failure event comprises an indication of a risk of the heart failure event," as recited by claims 3 and 20. The Office Action cited paragraphs [1409]-[1410] of Stahmann as allegedly disclosing this feature. However, paragraphs [1409]-[1410] of Stahmann do not mention risk or heart failure, and instead describe determining presence or absence of a disease or disorder. For example, paragraph [1410] describes "[i]f changes in the conditions indicative of physiological changes or symptoms caused by the disease are consistent with threshold levels, a presence of the disease or disorder may be determined."

For at least these reasons, the Office Action failed to establish a primafacie case for non- patentability of Applicant's claims 1, 3-18, and 20-30 under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
Applicant has added new claims 31 and 32. The applied references fail to disclose or suggest the recitations of new claims 31 and 32. No new matter is added by way of claims 31 and 32.
CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
